# A node's `#id` names the instance its argument list is building, so an
# argument of that list may not read it. The checker says so, with a position.
#
# This file used to pin the opposite: the fold's re-entry guard left such a
# prop standing and html wrote no <title> for it, silently, which CLAUDE.md
# recorded as the survivable answer rather than the right one. This is the
# right one for the half a node's id covers. `const a int = a` is the same
# shape one layer down and is a scope of its own, still accepted by `sngl
# check` and still guarded in consteval (const_reads_itself.txt).
! sngl check selfref.sngl
stderr 'names the node this argument list declares'
! sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out selfref.sngl

# Mutual reference is not reached by that rule and is not meant to be: neither
# window reads its own id, so what the two name is each other and there is no
# single declaration to blame. It reaches the fold's guard by a second key
# rather than by the first one twice, which is the path a self-reference never
# took, and it is still left standing -- the page comes out with content and no
# <title>. The general rule the language has not made is this one.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out2 mutual.sngl
grep '<span>a</span>' out2/a.html
grep '<span>b</span>' out2/b.html
! grep '<title>' out2/a.html
! grep '<title>' out2/b.html

-- selfref.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

window #home(title=home.title, href="/index.html") {
    text(value="hi")
}
-- mutual.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

component pages root {
    window #a(title=b.title, href="/a.html") {
        text(value="a")
    }
    window #b(title=a.title, href="/b.html") {
        text(value="b")
    }
}

pages()
